questions.q: According to this lesson, where does the raw data for this capstone ideally come from?
options: The three sources landed in the Snowflake course's own capstone (or three sources of similarly different shapes), already sitting in a raw schema
A brand-new production database that must be provisioned from scratch
This capstone does not use any raw data at all
A single flat CSV file with no other source types
questions.explain: This project picks up right where the Snowflake capstone left off, rebuilding that hand-written SQL transformation as a real dbt project against the same raw sources.

questions.q: Which of these is part of the capstone's full deliverable list, according to this lesson?
options: A staging model per source, at least one intermediate model, and a marts layer with a fact and a dimension model
Only a single flat model with no layering at all
A brand-new data warehouse platform built from scratch
Skipping tests entirely since it's a capstone project
questions.explain: The brief requires the full layering pattern from Chapters 2-3: sources, staging, intermediate, and marts.

questions.q: What does this lesson say happens to this exact project later in the catalog?
options: It's the same project the Git/GitHub/CI-CD course's own capstone picks up afterward and wires into a real CI/CD pipeline
It gets deleted once this course ends
It has nothing to do with any other course
It becomes a Power BI-only project with no dbt code retained
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly tells you to build this project like it's going to be reused, because the Git/GitHub/CI-CD course's capstone reuses it directly.

questions.q: What is the recommended order of operations for this capstone, according to this lesson?
options: Sources and staging first, then correct transformation logic, then tests and docs, then snapshot/incremental, then Power BI last
Connect Power BI first, then figure out the data afterward
Write all the tests before any models exist
There is no recommended order — build everything simultaneously
questions.explain: The lesson lays out a specific sequence: you can't test or document models that don't exist yet, and connecting BI only makes sense against a stable, tested marts layer.

questions.q: What does this lesson suggest as an optional nod to Chapter 8's semantic layer material?
options: Defining one metric on top of the marts layer using semantic layer concepts, though it isn't required for "done"
Rebuilding the entire capstone using only the semantic layer, skipping models entirely
Chapter 8 has no relevance to this capstone at all
Replacing all marts models with metrics definitions
questions.explain: The lesson calls this a stretch goal — not required, but the most direct way to prove you understood why the semantic layer chapter exists.
